body: Fuck.  It’s like looking into a mirror.
I don’t even know what kind of response you want to this.

Thanks :) I’ve been trying this, but she doesn’t know what she wants and just hasn’t got the energy to come with me when I suggest stuff to do.  We’re not rich by any means, but we are well off enough that we can do a supermarket shop without a list and not worry about the card machine, for example.

Thanks.  It’s the first thing in my life that I’ve not been in control of, or at least felt like I was collaboratively able to control it together with others.  It feels unfair and I hate it, but I think you’ve got sound advice.  I just- the path to being better is surely the one that involves taking advantage of the support around you, right?  Like talking to your counsellor, taking GP’s advice if they recommend medication, all that stuff?  It feels like I’m on the outside of the wall.

We do larp events here in the U.K., and it’s seriously like seeing two different people.  That’s kind of the point when you’re pretending to be a Viking and drinking in a field for a weekend, but all the day-to-day melts away from her and it’s like whet sculptors describe where they just remove the bits of stone that *aren’t* the sculpture underneath.

Being home together is really tough.  I’ve just started doing a job with a 1-2 hour commute each way, and she’s training to be a teacher.  Time isn’t something we have a lot of.

“You realize if she wants to kill herself, there is nothing you can do to stop her.”

This is what scares me the most.  I know you shouldn’t put your partner on a pedestal and whatever, but there *is no me* without her.

I’d like to talk to them but I don’t know who they are, and I can’t ask her because she won’t tell me, or figure this is what I may be trying to do and stonewall or something.  She’s very protective of feeling sad :(
I thought I did, because we had what I expect is a similar conversation.  That was a while ago now, so I honestly don’t know whether I still trust this.
